correctness.rationale: For Haar-independent points on an orthogonal flat three-torus, coordinate-wise shortest difference is uniform in [−a_i/2,a_i/2]. Thus D² has law ∑x_i U_i², x_i=a_i²/4. Independent exact rational cumulants of U² are 1/3,4/45,16/945; m1,m2,m3 determine power sums p1..p3 and Newton cubic with the three positive roots x_i. The discriminant Δ≥0 and e1,e2,e3>0 are necessary and sufficient even with repeated roots. Two moments fix plane-sphere intersection, a circle except at x1=x2=x3. The bounded-coefficient perturbation/Rouché argument matches three sorted roots within O(epsilon^(1/3)); an explicit near-cubic two-family collision has exact identical p1,p2 and p3 difference 2t³/√3, so any larger uniform exponent fails. Independently verified cumulant fractions and collision identities using exact rationals/symbolic algebra; the root-matching theorem is the genuine infinite analytic argument, not a finite sample.
